## Source-specific reading

The chapter explains the significance of the sanctuary of earth-born Erechtheus on the Acropolis. The olive and sea are presented as the Athenians’ reported witnesses of the rival gods. The narrative then reports the burning and what the Athenians commanded to sacrifice saw on the following day: a shoot about one cubit long. Its final act is their reporting.

The nested report matters. This is the testimony of a narrated sacred place, not independent confirmation of miraculous regrowth. Nor does the sanctuary before the burning identify every feature of the later Erechtheion. Pausanias supplies a separate regrowth tradition.
